text: dsh-leader-agent 是面向 DSH 的多智能体项目编排插件，提供 Leader 与 worker 会话、项目树和右侧交付看板。Leader 可创建任务卡、派发并跟进 worker，worker 完成后自动回报；项目规则与角色说明可由 LEADER.md 和 SLOTS.md 注入。看板按项目汇总任务状态与链接，适合需要并行推进和审阅多项工作的 DSH 用户。需在长驻的 web、desktop 或 SDK 宿主中使用。

dsh-leader-agent adds project based worker orchestration to DSH. A Leader creates task cards, dispatches persistent workers, sends follow ups, and receives completion reports. Its web board tracks project tasks and links workers to their sessions.

dsh-leader-agent 的功能「后台派工」：Leader 可创建 worker 会话，再通过消息投递任务；worker 完成一轮后会向 Leader 自动回报。
dsh-leader-agent 的功能「项目任务卡」：Leader 可创建、更新和列出任务卡，记录规格、状态、执行槽位与链接，供项目成员跟进交付。
dsh-leader-agent 的功能「交付看板」：在项目会话的右侧看板查看活动与已完成任务，打开卡片详情或进入对应 worker 会话继续沟通。

dsh-leader-agent README · dsh-leader-agent：> One Leader drives the work and the review, so you can run ten features in parallel instead of babysitting each one.
>
> A leader / worker orchestration bundle for DeepSeek Harness (dsh). The Leader splits work, dispatches it, tracks every worker to completion, checks what comes back and runs review; workers do the work in the background, report back automatically, and every task fact lands on a board organized by project. Running one worktree per task is this repository's convention, not a requirement of the bundle.

dsh-leader-agent README · Highlights：1. **One Leader drives development and review** — You state the goal once. The Leader opens cards, dispatches workers, watches each one finish, verifies the deliverable and organizes review. Your attention goes back to "what do I want" instead of "which agent is stuck"; the target is ten features in flight at once.
2. **A right SidePanel board: see who is working at a glance** — One board per project. Each card carries its executor slot and a live status light, its note renders as Markdown, and its links are editable in place. Click a card for the spec (goal, scope, acceptance, links), click a slot to drill into that agent's session and keep talking; worker reports arrive as the worker speaking, also Markdown-rendered.
3. **Arrange your agents however you want** — Two files do the arranging. `LEADER.md` holds the Leader's prompt and this project's orchestration rules: boundaries, dispatch requirements, acceptance criteria. `SLOTS.md` gives each worker role its own rules (dev / review / …). Both are evaluated before every model request and appended only when their text changes, so editing a file changes behavior without recreating sessions.

dsh-leader-agent README · Web install：Install from npm (package name `dsh-leader-agent`):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-leader-agent
dsh web
```

The profile must be named `web`; custom names are absent from `PROFILE_TEMPLATES`, so the install lacks the web-app bundle and the client half never loads. Requires dsh `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0`.

For pinning a version, removing it, development installs, or trying it without a profile, see [Development](docs/development.md).

dsh-leader-agent README · Upgrading from `dsh-leader-kit`：The package was renamed to `dsh-leader-agent` **without a compatibility path**. `dsh plugin add` records the *package name* in `dsh.profile.bundles`, so the old entry survives and both bundles get applied: tools registered twice, two dispatchers settling the same `turn/end` (duplicate notifications and wakeups). Remove the old entry first, in the same profile you install into:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-leader-kit
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-leader-agent
```

dsh-leader-agent README · Upgrading from `dsh-leader-kit`：The data directory moved with the name (`$DSH_HOME/dsh-leader-kit` → `$DSH_HOME/dsh-leader-agent`) and is **not migrated**: boards start empty and worker registrations rebuild on first start. The old package is deprecated in favor of this one.

dsh-leader-agent README · How it runs：```text
you ──────▶ Leader (the leader session, sole commander of the project)
             │  create_card      record what to build and how it is accepted
             │  spawn_worker     create the worker session, return immediately
             │  message_worker   deliver the first message — that is what starts work

Three mechanisms make this more than "a smarter prompt":

dsh-leader-agent README · How it runs：- **Identity decides the tool surface.** The Leader gets `spawn_worker` / `message_worker`; workers don't. The host trims the tool surface when a session is created — the model is not trusted to hold back.
- **Completion is settled by the runtime, which wakes the Leader.** When a worker's turn ends, the Leader receives a report (rendered as the worker speaking), with no polling from the Leader and no submit step from the worker.
- **Workers are persistent root sessions.** Several run at once, you can open any of them and keep the conversation going, and they cold-resume after a restart. The cost: the Leader cannot stop one, see [Current limitations](#current-limitations).

dsh-leader-agent README · Design trade-offs：- This project does not aim to rebuild dsh's own super agent. It solves one concrete problem: letting one person manage 20+ sessions.
- Today's agents are not reliable enough to run unattended, so the design assumes you can interrupt or push any worker at any point.
- The routing layer runs a full-size model. In practice, holding the global picture, it often connects several PRs in one thought and resolves what a single worker cannot see.
- Agent orchestration generalizes. A card describes the task itself, so it works outside coding and composes with any skill.
- Initialization is still manual: in your own project you write `LEADER.md` (the Leader's persona prompt and orchestration flow) and `SLOTS.md` (the role split and each role's persona prompt).
- The Leader leads and workers never talk to each other; the tool surface rules it out. Today's agents are trained for strict instruction-following, and one noisy message between two agents can derail the entire conversation.

dsh-leader-agent README · Five steps：1. **Add a project.** In the left sidebar's Projects section, click Add project and pick a directory. The project is created immediately and bound to a leader session; clicking the project row opens that Leader. Selection comes in two layers: the whole row only lights up for the current Leader session, while opening a worker lights the row-start glyph and puts the row highlight on that worker's own session row. The slot at the row start shows the host's `apps-add-outline` glyph by default (three cells plus a plus sign; it replaces the host's folder icon so projects and workspaces are not the same shape in the sidebar): while the Leader is running it becomes a spinner (the Leader has no row of its own, so this holds whether the project is expanded or collapsed), and when the project is collapsed with a worker running under it, it becomes a spinner too — once expanded, each worker carries its own spinner.
2. **Load the protocol.** In the leader session, have the model load `leader-mode`. It reads `playbooks/program.md` first, then the playbook for the current stage.

dsh-leader-agent README · Orchestration lives in files：Three things, each covering one layer. All of them contribute prompt text only and grant no tool permissions:

dsh-leader-agent README · Orchestration lives in files：| File / skill | For whom | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `LEADER.md` | The Leader of this project | How to command this project: boundaries, card and dispatch granularity, hard constraints every brief must carry, acceptance criteria. Injected into the leader session, with no binding step |
| `SLOTS.md` | Workers, by role | Per-role method and persona under `## <slot-name>` (`dev` / `review` / …). The card's `slots` field binds a slot to a session, and that session gets the section injected |
| `leader-mode` skill | The Leader's protocol | Staged playbooks for discussion → design → implementation and delivery → review → merge, plus parallel-collaboration and handoff guidance |

dsh-leader-agent README · Orchestration lives in files：`LEADER.md` and `SLOTS.md` are evaluated before every model request and appended only when their text changes, so a change takes effect on the next request and nothing gets injected twice. The `leader-mode` skill takes a different path — the model loads it through the `skill` tool on demand, which is why the step above says load rather than configure. The target project's own `AGENTS.md` is read by the host's agent-instructions as a system-prompt section. Closing a card (`done` / `archived`) releases its executor: the slot binding and the card facts stop being injected together.

dsh-leader-agent README · Orchestration lives in files：The plugin only reads `LEADER.md`. A `COORDINATOR.md` that merely points at it is a compatibility shim for external tools that still look for the old file name; it is never injected, and you do not need it otherwise.

Slot names are ASCII identifiers (lowercase letters, digits, underscore, hyphen, up to 32 characters); display names come from the `slots:` frontmatter at the top of `SLOTS.md`. A project without `SLOTS.md` falls back to the default two roles `dev` / `review`.

dsh-leader-agent README · Orchestration lives in files：The `init-leader-agent` skill handles project setup: it merges the repository's engineering conventions into a managed block of the target project's `AGENTS.md`, then writes `LEADER.md` (how the Leader drives this project) and `SLOTS.md` (executor roles) from the bundled skeletons. Re-running only replaces the managed block, and both manuals are read before editing. An empty directory gets the TODO skeleton plus the three questions still unanswered — project facts are never invented.

dsh-leader-agent README · Orchestration lives in files：For the full interaction — slot frontmatter details, archiving, swapping the Leader, how board status lights are derived — see the [usage manual](docs/usage.md) (Chinese).

dsh-leader-agent README · Prerequisites: get multi-worktree parallelism working first：Running ten features in parallel requires real isolation between tasks: one worktree per task, one dsh instance per task, one data root per task, so tasks never overwrite each other's plugin version or compete for sessions and data. This repository's `scripts/worktree-*.mjs` and `scripts/dev.mjs` exist for exactly this ([Development](docs/development.md)); mechanisms and where each one lands are in [collaboration and documentation](docs/architecture.md#协作与文档机制) (Chinese).

dsh-leader-agent README · Current limitations：- **Background orchestration needs a long-lived host** (web / desktop / sdk). headless is a one-shot CLI: the session is destroyed when the turn ends, and nothing is left to receive completion reports.
- **The Leader cannot stop a worker.** Workers are ordinary root sessions, so the host's `list_agents` / `send_message` / `interrupt_agent` do not apply to them (`interrupt_agent` even returns a false success). A worker that goes off track has to be handled by a human in its own session. That is the price of persistence. You can read what it is doing (`read_worker_session`, read-only, no wake-up), but you cannot act for it or call it off.
- **Completion reports depend on the turn ending normally.** If the process dies before a worker finishes, that turn is never settled. After a restart, open the worker session and continue there.
- **The board only shows for project sessions.** The leader and that project's workers see it; an ordinary session in the same directory, or a retired leader, only gets a notice, and sessions outside any project get no board at all.
